She is running flat out along the surface with a brimming shell held dead level in both hands, wings sealed shut, a single bee riding her shoulder like it bought a seat.
The near fae has both arms wrapped round a whole pale slab and is leaning back into nothing, heels at the rim, trusting her weight to stop it going over the edge.
He peels a broad wax lid back in one piece, whole body arched into it, and the honey beneath catches his chin before he is ready for it.
She blows hard on a smouldering bundle, cheeks round as fruit, her other hand shoved flat against the air as though that will move it faster.
Two of them haul a dripping slab in a slung leaf-cloth between them, both leaning back hard, one walking in reverse and already running out of surface behind her.
The near fae has her whole arm buried in a broken slab up to the shoulder and is using her free hand to shield her face from the mass boiling above.
She lowers a loaded shell on a twisted grass-cord, one foot hooked round the rim for anchor, watching it drop toward the drop with her whole body canted sideways.
He sits on the rim with both feet over the drop eating a sealed slab with both hands, a bee orbiting his head and him paying it no attention at all.
She stops dead mid-step, shell tipped at a dangerous angle in one hand, staring at something directly ahead that has changed the entire plan.
The near fae plugs a cracked shell with a dab of resin, pressing it flat with her thumb, honey still moving through her fingers while she works.
A second grown fae catches her by the scruff with one arm and hauls back while she strains forward over the drop, shell still clutched and dripping.
She is nose to nose with one bee, both stopped dead, the cupped shell hanging forgotten at full stretch from her other hand, honey threading off the rim.
He wedges himself into a hollow beside the wax with only his boots and a full shell visible, and the full shell is already tilting.
She swings in on a grass-cord line, smouldering bundle thrust ahead at arm's length, legs tucked, the mass parting round her shoulders as she comes through.
One boot is stuck fast in spilt honey and she hauls on her own leg with both hands and her full weight, wings flung wide for balance, gaining nothing.
Two of them drink straight from a broken slab at the same time, faces in it, neither one watching the mass gathering above them both.
The near fae thumbs a wax cup free with one hand and licks her thumb while the other hand holds the shell ready, and the bees have opinions.
She holds a broad leaf flat over a second grown fae's head with both arms raised, standing into the boil above while the fae below works with her hands.
He slides down the outside of a tall wax sheet with both arms wrapped round it, a shell strapped across his back and filling as he goes.
She tips a broken slab over the shell and catches the pour with her whole body curved under it, one knee on the surface, one foot already off the edge.
The near fae stands back-to-back with a second grown fae, both arms spread wide, holding the mass off while the other one fills the shell behind her.
He is asleep flat on the surface, face down and amber from the ears to the chin, and one bee is sitting on the heel of his boot like a sentinel.
She wraps a grass-cord round a full slab twice, tests the knot with a hard jerk, and the slab lurches toward the drop before she has finished testing.
The near fae presses her palm over a crack in the wax, honey forcing up through every gap in her fingers, and she is solving this with the wrong hand.
A second grown fae leans the full length of her arm across a gap to take the brimming shell, her other hand clutching the rim and her feet off the surface.
